final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key evidentiary gap: there is still no proof that the required disclosure exists in final launch materials, no proof of exclusion of the affected use case, and no approved risk acceptance. The Actor's response is a narrower and more policy-faithful framing of the same record, not new support. That reframing improves precision, but the caveat is not merely descriptive; it is an unresolved compliance condition. Under the stated policy, rollout controls, monitoring, rollback, and a 3% launch do not cure disclosure duties while the affected segment remains exposed. On this record, a conditional statement about what would make certification supportable is more defensible than the original broader certification theory, but present compliance remains insufficiently supported.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the final model card or launch materials explicitly disclose the health-plan benefits support limitation.
The affected use case remains exposed in the rollout design on the available record.
There is still no approved risk acceptance covering continued exposure of that segment.
The actor's narrowed position is conditional on a policy predicate that remains unproven, so it does not establish present compliance.
